synopsis: The corpus cites Feng et al.’s Nature paper, published on 22 March 2023, as an on-road statistical-validation precedent using dense deep reinforcement learning (D2RL) [f426, f6848]. It reports evaluation accelerated by 10^3 to 10^5 times while remaining unbiased, demonstrated on highway and urban test tracks with an augmented-reality environment [f6848, f14163]. The method trained dense-reinforcement-learning background agents; Chapter 9 also describes the acceleration in terms of naturalistic-adversarial environments and dense RL [f633, f7276]. These results support accelerated automated-road-vehicle validation, but the corpus explicitly identifies a transfer gap: D2RL is proven only on-road, not for off-road testing [f351, f7079].
